summary: A metallic rust mat coating the basalt walls of flooded lava tubes and damp fissures (F9). It oxidises hydrogen sulfide from fumaroles using the abundant oxygen to fix carbon, forming a dense iron-sulfur crust (D22, F5). The film glitters with ochre and black flecks, providing a rare calorie source in the dark.

links: Fumarolic H2S seeps into flooded lava tubes (F9, D22)
High ambient O2 (F5) makes sulfur oxidation highly exergonic
Iron in basalt water oxidises to rust
Forms a thick, nutritious, yet toxic film
chains.play: Gift to *Sosa* to befriend; scrape for iron grit.
chains.weakness: Accumulates arsenic and mercury; causes poisoning if eaten raw.
observe: Serves as a navigational beacon for *Sosa* in the dark

plausibility.summary: Iron- and sulfur-oxidising biofilms on damp basalt in lava tubes fit D22, F9, and F5: O₂-rich cave air drives exergonic sulfur and Fe(II) oxidation, yielding rust-colored ochre crusts and a dark calorie source where light is absent.

analogues.mechanism: Microaerophilic Fe-oxidisers deposit Fe oxyhydroxide sheaths; co-occurring sulfur oxidisers use cave seeps (Emerson & Moyer, 2002, from memory, unverified). Arsenic and mercury co-precipitate or absorb on Fe phases as on Earth vent precipitates.

colour.base: Metallic rust-red with black speckles. Iron oxidation yields the ochre-red base (D22); dark inorganic polymers and sulfur compounds add the black flecks. No photosynthetic pigment; the colour signals high sulfur and iron content.
